schemes.title: Gruha Jyothi (Free Electricity up to 200 Units)
schemes.department: Energy Department, Government of Karnataka, through the electricity supply companies (BESCOM, MESCOM, CESC, HESCOM, GESCOM)
schemes.brief: Karnataka gives every household free electricity up to its usual monthly use, as long as that stays within 200 units. Your free limit is your average monthly use in 2022-23 plus 10 units. Use within that limit and the bill is zero; use more and you pay only for the extra units; cross 200 units in a month and you pay the full bill for that month. You register once, free, by linking the house's electricity account to your Aadhaar. Owners and tenants can both apply.
schemes.benefit: Zero bill up to your free limit (average 2022-23 use + 10 units), up to 200 units a month
eligibility: A domestic (house) electricity connection in Karnataka. Shops and other commercial use are not covered
Owner, tenant or family member living in the house. One connection per Aadhaar, and one connection per house
Monthly use must stay at or below 200 units. Above 200, the full bill is charged for that month
Free limit = average monthly use in 2022-23 plus 10 units. A new house or new connection with no 2022-23 record gets a fixed limit based on the state average of 53 units
Old unpaid electricity dues must be cleared. Homes on Bhagya Jyothi, Kutira Jyothi and Amrut Jyothi are included in Gruha Jyothi
documents: Aadhaar card of the person applying
Latest electricity bill, for the ESCOM name and the Account ID (connection ID)
Mobile number linked to Aadhaar, for the OTP
The bill need not be in your name: tenants and family members choose their type in the form
Tenants: a rent agreement or other proof of living at that address, if the office asks for it

demoFields.label: Preferred Language
demoFields.hint: English or Kannada. The labels of the form change to the language you pick.

demoFields.label: ESCOM name
demoFields.hint: The company named at the top of your bill: BESCOM, MESCOM, CESC, HESCOM, GESCOM or Hukkeri Society.

demoFields.label: Account ID
demoFields.hint: The account or connection ID printed on your bill, not the meter number. The name and address then fill in from the ESCOM's records.

demoFields.label: Account holder's name as in ESCOM
demoFields.hint: Comes from the ESCOM record. It may be the landlord's name or a late parent's name; that is fine.

demoFields.label: Account holder's address as in ESCOM
demoFields.hint: Filled in automatically. Check that it is the house you actually live in.

demoFields.label: User type
demoFields.hint: Owner, Tenant, or Family member (for example, when the bill is in your father's name).

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: Your own Aadhaar. One Aadhaar can be linked to only one connection in the whole state.

demoFields.label: Applicant's name
demoFields.hint: Exactly as on your Aadhaar. The OTP check matches it.

demoFields.label: Phone number for communication
demoFields.hint: The acknowledgement and later messages about the scheme come here.

demoFields.label: Declaration
demoFields.hint: You confirm the connection is used only for the house. Commercial use cancels the benefit, and the free amount is recovered with interest.

demoSteps: Keep your latest electricity bill ready and find the ESCOM name and the Account ID on it.

Open sevasindhugs.karnataka.gov.in, choose Gruha Jyothi and click to register. The form opens without any login. A Grama One, Karnataka One or Bangalore One centre, or your ESCOM office, will also register you free.
Select your ESCOM, type the Account ID and check the name and address that appear. Choose Owner, Tenant or Family member, then enter your Aadhaar and verify it with the OTP.
Tick the declaration, submit, and note the acknowledgement number. You can check the status later on the Seva Sindhu 'Track Status' page.
From the next bill, your bill shows your free limit (eligible units). Within it the bill is zero; above it you pay only for the extra units; above 200 units you pay the whole bill.
Tenants moving house: use the Gruha Jyothi De-link option on the same portal to free your Aadhaar from the old connection, then register again at the new house.
If the bill is not zero, first check the eligible-units line on it, then call 1912 or visit the ESCOM sub-division office with your acknowledgement number.
schemes.helpline: 1912 — ESCOM electricity helpline (24x7); 1902 — Karnataka guarantee schemes helpline; 080-22279954 / 87926 62814 — guarantee scheme application help

schemes.title: Shakti Yojana (Free Bus Travel for Women)
schemes.department: Transport Department, Government of Karnataka — KSRTC, BMTC, KKRTC and NWKRTC
schemes.brief: Women and girls who live in Karnataka, and transgender persons, travel free in ordinary government buses anywhere inside the state. There is no form, card or registration: show a government photo ID with a Karnataka address to the conductor and you get a zero-fare Shakti ticket. Air-conditioned and luxury buses, sleeper buses and buses that cross into another state are not free.
schemes.benefit: Free travel in ordinary and express non-AC government buses within Karnataka
eligibility: Women and girls of any age who live in Karnataka, including school and college students
Transgender persons who live in Karnataka
No income, caste or age limit, and nothing to apply for
Covers ordinary and express non-AC buses of KSRTC, BMTC, KKRTC and NWKRTC, including non-AC electric buses
Not covered: Rajahamsa, AC buses such as Airavat, Vajra, Vayu Vajra, Ambaari and Flybus, sleeper buses, and interstate routes, even for the Karnataka part of the trip
documents: Aadhaar card, or
Voter ID, driving licence, passport, or MGNREGA job card with photo and address
Photo ID with address issued by a Government of India or Karnataka department or a public sector company
ID card from the Department for the Empowerment of Differently Abled and Senior Citizens, or a transgender ID card
School or college ID card, for girl students
The original, a photocopy, or the DigiLocker copy (printed or on the phone) is accepted
schemes.submitAt: There is no form and nowhere to apply. Board an ordinary or express non-AC bus of KSRTC, BMTC, KKRTC or NWKRTC on a route inside Karnataka, show the conductor an ID with your photo and Karnataka address (original, photocopy or DigiLocker copy), and ask for the Shakti ticket.

demoFields.label: Corporation
demoFields.hint: Printed at the top of the ticket. KSRTC, BMTC, KKRTC and NWKRTC buses are all covered.

demoFields.label: Type of bus
demoFields.hint: Ordinary, express and non-AC electric buses are free. Rajahamsa, AC, sleeper and Flybus services are not.

demoFields.label: Boarding point
demoFields.hint: Tell the conductor where you got on.

demoFields.label: Destination
demoFields.hint: Must be inside Karnataka. On a bus going to another state you pay the full fare.

demoFields.label: ID shown
demoFields.hint: Any government photo ID that shows a Karnataka address.

demoFields.label: Passengers
demoFields.hint: Each woman and girl gets her own zero ticket. Men travelling with you buy normal tickets.

demoFields.label: Ticket type
demoFields.hint: Keep it until you get down. Checking staff can ask for it.

demoFields.label: Fare value printed
demoFields.hint: The ticket shows what the trip would have cost. The state pays this amount to the bus company.

demoSteps: Carry one ID with your photo and Karnataka address. Aadhaar is the easiest; a photocopy or the DigiLocker copy on your phone is also accepted.
Board an ordinary or express non-AC government bus. Check the name on the front: Rajahamsa, Airavat, Vajra, Vayu Vajra, Ambaari, Flybus and sleeper buses are not free.
Tell the conductor your destination, show the ID and ask for the Shakti ticket.
Take the zero-fare ticket and keep it until you get down. A passenger without a ticket can be fined even on a free trip.
On KSRTC, KKRTC and NWKRTC buses half the seats are kept for men; BMTC city buses have no such split.
If a conductor refuses the free ticket on a covered bus, note the bus number, route and time, and complain to that corporation's helpline.
schemes.helpline: KSRTC call centre (24x7): 080-26252625; BMTC helpline: 080-22483777; 1902 — Karnataka guarantee schemes helpline

schemes.title: Yuva Nidhi (Unemployment Allowance for Graduates and Diploma Holders)
schemes.department: Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood Department (Department of Employment and Training), Government of Karnataka
schemes.brief: Karnataka pays a monthly allowance to young people who finished a degree or diploma and still have no job six months after the result: Rs.3,000 a month for graduates and postgraduates, Rs.1,500 for diploma holders. It is paid for up to two years, or until you get a job or start further studies, whichever comes first. You apply on Seva Sindhu (now Seva One), and you must confirm on the portal every three months that you are still unemployed, or the payment stops.
schemes.benefit: Rs.3,000 a month for graduates, Rs.1,500 a month for diploma holders, for up to 2 years
eligibility: Passed a degree, postgraduate degree or diploma from the 2022-23 academic year onward
No job (government or private) and not self-employed for 180 days after the result
Karnataka domicile: studied in Karnataka for at least 6 years, counting SSLC, PUC and the degree or diploma
Not studying further, not drawing an apprenticeship stipend, and not getting any other unemployment allowance
A bank account in your own name, seeded with Aadhaar
documents: Aadhaar card, with the mobile number linked to it for the OTP
Degree, postgraduate or diploma marks cards and the provisional or final certificate
SSLC and PUC marks cards, as proof of study in Karnataka
Bank passbook of an account in your own name, Aadhaar-seeded
Mobile number and email ID
Self-declaration that you are not employed or studying (made on the portal)

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: Your own Aadhaar. Your name, date of birth and photo are taken from it after the OTP.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: Payment messages and the three-monthly declaration reminders come here.

demoFields.label: Qualification
demoFields.hint: Graduates and postgraduates get Rs.3,000; diploma holders get Rs.1,500. Choose what you actually passed.

demoFields.label: University / Board
demoFields.hint: The body that awarded the degree or diploma.

demoFields.label: Register number / USN
demoFields.hint: As printed on your final marks card.

demoFields.label: Year and date of result
demoFields.hint: The 180 days without a job are counted from this date. Apply only after they are over.

demoFields.label: SSLC and PUC register numbers and years
demoFields.hint: These prove that you studied in Karnataka.

demoFields.label: Are you employed, self-employed or studying?
demoFields.hint: Answer truthfully. Money paid on a false answer is recovered.

demoFields.label: Bank account number and IFSC
demoFields.hint: Your own account, NPCI-seeded with Aadhaar, or the transfer fails.

demoFields.label: District / Taluk
demoFields.hint: Where you live. The district employment officer handles your file.

demoSteps: Wait until 180 days have passed since your result date, with no job and no further studies.

Open the Yuva Nidhi service on Seva One (sevaone.karnataka.gov.in), log in or register with your mobile number and OTP, and complete the Aadhaar e-KYC. A Grama One, Karnataka One or Bangalore One centre can do this for you.
Fill in your qualification, register number, year of passing and SSLC and PUC details, upload the marks cards, and give your Aadhaar-seeded bank account.
Submit and note the application number. The district employment officer checks your certificates; follow it with 'Yuvanidhi Application Status Check' on the portal.
Once approved, the allowance is paid into your account every month by DBT. The department may also ask you to register on the Kaushalkar skills portal for training.
Every three months, submit the 'Unemployment Self Declaration' on the portal. If you miss it, the payment stops until you submit it.
When you get a job or join a course, stop declaring. The allowance ends after two years in any case.
schemes.helpline: 1902 — Karnataka guarantee schemes helpline; 080-22279954 / 87926 62814 / 87926 62816 — Seva Sindhu application and technical help

schemes.title: Ayushman Bharat – Arogya Karnataka (AB-ArK Health Card)
schemes.department: Department of Health and Family Welfare, Government of Karnataka — Suvarna Arogya Suraksha Trust (SAST)
schemes.brief: Karnataka's health cover, run together with the central Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY. Families with a BPL (Priority Household or Antyodaya) ration card get free treatment up to Rs.5 lakh a year for the whole family; other families get 30% of the treatment cost paid, up to Rs.1.5 lakh a year. Treatment starts at a government hospital, which refers you to a listed private hospital if it cannot treat you; listed emergencies can go straight to a listed hospital. The card is made at a government hospital counter for Rs.10 with your Aadhaar and ration card.
schemes.benefit: BPL families: up to Rs.5 lakh a year free; other families: 30% of the cost, up to Rs.1.5 lakh a year
eligibility: Every resident of Karnataka with an Aadhaar card can enrol
Eligible category (free treatment up to Rs.5 lakh per family per year): families with a Priority Household (BPL) or Antyodaya ration card under the Food Security Act
General category (APL card or no ration card): the government pays 30% of the package rate, up to Rs.1.5 lakh per family per year, and the family pays the rest
Simpler treatments are given only in government hospitals. A private hospital needs a referral from a government hospital, except for the listed emergencies
Aadhaar authentication is compulsory before a referral to a private hospital
documents: Aadhaar card of the patient (each member of the family enrols separately)
Ration card, which decides whether you are in the eligible or the general category
Mobile number, for the SMS with your ArK ID
Rs.10 for the card (Rs.20 for a reprint if it is lost)
Referral letter from the government hospital, when going to a private hospital
Earlier prescriptions, test reports and discharge papers, if any
schemes.submitAt: At the registration (Arogya Mitra) counter of any government hospital: Primary Health Centre, Community Health Centre, taluk or district hospital, or medical college hospital. Take every member's Aadhaar card and the ration card, and Rs.10 per card. Grama One, Karnataka One and Bangalore One centres also issue the card.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: The patient's own Aadhaar. Each family member is enrolled one by one.

demoFields.label: Authentication
demoFields.hint: Fingerprint on the biometric device. If it fails, the staff can use an OTP to the Aadhaar mobile or the QR code on the Aadhaar card.

demoFields.label: Ration card (PDS) number
demoFields.hint: From the ration card. It links you to your family in the food department's records.

demoFields.label: Category
demoFields.hint: Filled automatically: Priority Household or Antyodaya card = Eligible; APL card or no card = General.

demoFields.label: Name, gender and age
demoFields.hint: Taken from the Aadhaar e-KYC. Check the spelling before the card is printed.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: Your ArK ID is sent here by SMS.

demoFields.label: District / Taluk
demoFields.hint: Where you live.

demoFields.label: Consent and self-declaration
demoFields.value: Signed — no other health insurance scheme
demoFields.hint: A printed form: you allow your Aadhaar to be used for enrolment and state that you are not covered by another scheme.

demoFields.label: ArK ID (generated)
demoFields.hint: Your ration card number, a dash and your member number. It is printed on the card.

demoFields.label: Card fee
demoFields.hint: Paid once. A reprint of a lost card costs Rs.20.

demoSteps: Go to the registration counter of a government hospital (PHC, CHC, taluk or district hospital) with your Aadhaar and ration card.
The staff check your Aadhaar by fingerprint (or OTP or QR code), and your ration card decides your category: Eligible (BPL) or General.
Sign the consent and self-declaration, pay Rs.10, and collect the printed card with your ArK ID. Repeat this for each family member.
When you fall ill, go first to a government hospital. If it cannot give the treatment, ask the doctor for a referral to a private hospital empanelled under AB-ArK.
At the private hospital, go to the Arogya Mitra desk with the card, your Aadhaar and the referral letter. The hospital takes approval from SAST; for eligible families the treatment is cashless.
In an emergency covered by the listed emergency procedures, go straight to the nearest empanelled hospital. No referral is needed.
If a hospital asks a BPL card holder to pay for a covered treatment, call 104 or 1800 425 8330 before paying.
schemes.helpline: 104 — Arogya Sahayavani (toll free); 1800 425 8330 — Arogya Karnataka helpline

schemes.title: Karnataka Construction Workers Labour Card (KBOCWWB e-Card)
schemes.department: Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Labour Department, Government of Karnataka
schemes.brief: Construction workers in Karnataka who register with the Welfare Board get a labour card, now a digital e-card, which opens the board's help: Rs.50,000 for each of a woman worker's first two deliveries, Rs.60,000 for a marriage, up to Rs.2 lakh for a major illness, education help for children, accident cover and a pension at 60. You register on the board's Karmika Seva Kendra (KSK) portal with your Aadhaar mobile number and a 90-day work certificate. Workers who already hold an old Seva Sindhu or e-Karmika card move it to the new portal with their registration and reference numbers.
schemes.benefit: Labour e-card for board help: Rs.50,000 per delivery, Rs.60,000 for marriage, up to Rs.2 lakh medical aid, pension up to Rs.3,000 a month at 60
eligibility: Aged 18 to 60
Worked at least 90 days as a building or construction worker in the last 12 months: mason, helper, carpenter, painter, plumber, electrician, bar bender, tile layer and similar work
Working in Karnataka
The e-card is valid for one year. Renew it on the portal with a fresh work certificate, or the benefits stop
For the pension, you must have been registered for at least 3 years before turning 60
documents: Aadhaar card, and the mobile number linked to it
90-day work certificate in the board's format, signed by your employer or contractor, a registered construction workers' union, or the labour inspector
Ration card number and a copy of the card
Bank passbook of the worker and of the nominee (account number and IFSC)
Nominee's details, and the nominee's own application number if the nominee is also a construction worker
Educational certificate, only if you studied beyond SSLC
Ayushman Bharat card number, if you have one
Your old Seva Sindhu or e-Karmika card, if you already have one

demoFields.label: Registration type
demoFields.value: Register as a New Construction Worker
demoFields.hint: If you already have an old card, choose 'Already Existing Seva Sindhu/E-Karmika Construction Worker' instead and type its registration and reference numbers exactly as printed.

demoFields.label: Mobile number linked to Aadhaar
demoFields.hint: The OTP comes here. The Aadhaar e-KYC then fills in your name, date of birth and photo.

demoFields.label: Caste, religion and education
demoFields.hint: An education certificate is needed only if you studied beyond SSLC.

demoFields.label: Present address
demoFields.hint: Where you live now, if it is different from the address on Aadhaar.

demoFields.label: Family and nominee
demoFields.value: Wife Renuka (31), son Kiran (9), daughter Pooja (6)
demoFields.hint: The nominee receives the death and funeral help. Add your children too; education and marriage help is given for them.

demoFields.label: Bank account and IFSC (worker and nominee)
demoFields.hint: Aadhaar-seeded accounts. Upload the passbook page for each.

demoFields.label: Ration card number
demoFields.hint: Upload a copy of the card as well.

demoFields.label: Employer / owner details
demoFields.hint: Name of the employer, the company, and the mobile number of the person in charge of the site.

demoFields.label: Work site address and PIN code
demoFields.hint: Where you did the 90 days of work.

demoFields.label: Nature of work and certificate issuer
demoFields.value: Mason — certificate by a registered construction workers' union
demoFields.hint: Upload the 90-day certificate and the self-declaration. The labour inspector checks them, sometimes at the site.

demoSteps: Get the 90-day work certificate in the board's format (the KSK portal has the template), signed by your employer or contractor, a registered construction workers' union, or the labour inspector.

Open kbocwwb.karnataka.gov.in, choose Apply for Registration, select 'Register as a New Construction Worker' and verify your Aadhaar-linked mobile with the OTP. Without a smartphone, go to the Karmika Seva Kendra or labour inspector's office in your taluk.
Fill in your personal, family, nominee, bank and work details as in this sample, and upload the documents (JPG, PNG or PDF, up to 2 MB each).
Submit and note the acknowledgement number. The labour inspector checks your documents and may visit the work site.
Once approved, download your e-card (digital labour ID) from your KSK dashboard.
Apply for help (delivery, marriage, medical, pension) from the same dashboard. For your children's education help, apply on the State Scholarship Portal, ssp.karnataka.gov.in.
Renew before the e-card expires: log in, and enter your current employer, work site and a new work certificate. The portal reminds you 15 days before expiry.
schemes.helpline: 155214 — Construction Workers Welfare Board helpline (toll free)

schemes.title: Karnataka Social Security Pensions (Old Age, Sandhya Suraksha, Widow and Disability Pension)
schemes.department: Directorate of Social Security and Pensions, Revenue Department, Government of Karnataka
schemes.brief: Karnataka pays a monthly pension to poor elderly people, widows and people with disabilities, straight into a bank or post office account. The old age pension is Rs.600 a month from 60 to 64 and Rs.1,200 from 65; Sandhya Suraksha gives Rs.1,200 to farmers, labourers, weavers and fishermen aged 65 and above; widows get Rs.800; people with disabilities get Rs.800 to Rs.2,000. One common form covers all of them, and you hand it in at the Atalji Janasnehi Kendra (Nadakacheri) for your area.
schemes.benefit: Rs.600 to Rs.2,000 a month depending on the pension; Rs.1,200 for most people aged 65 and above
eligibility: Resident of Karnataka, with a family income below Rs.32,000 a year
Old age pension (IGNOAPS): BPL, aged 60 or above. Rs.600 a month at 60 to 64, Rs.1,200 at 65 and above

Sandhya Suraksha: aged 65 or above; small or marginal farmer, farm labourer, weaver, fisherman or unorganised worker (not construction-board workers); husband and wife's deposits together not above Rs.10,000. Rs.1,200 a month
Widow pension: destitute widow aged 18 to 64. Rs.800 a month, until remarriage or a job that takes income above the limit
Disability pension: 40% disability or more, certified by a medical board, Rs.800; 75% or more, Rs.1,400; 75% or more mental disability, Rs.2,000
Not already drawing another pension. Having sons does not disqualify you if they do not support you
documents: The filled application form
Aadhaar card
Age proof: birth certificate, voter ID with date of birth, or a doctor's age certificate
Residence certificate
Income certificate (below Rs.32,000 a year)
Bank or post office passbook, first page
Ration card
As needed: husband's death certificate (widow), medical board disability certificate (disability), occupation certificate from the Tahsildar (Sandhya Suraksha)
schemes.submitAt: The Atalji Janasnehi Kendra (Nadakacheri counter) at your hobli or taluk office. Take the filled form, signed or with your thumb impression, with copies of Aadhaar, age proof, residence and income certificates, the bank or post office passbook and the ration card, plus the death, disability or occupation certificate your pension needs. The counter charges a small service fee; ask for the printed acknowledgement.

demoFields.label: District / Taluk / Hobli / Village
demoFields.hint: Written at the top of the form. It decides which village officer verifies your application.

demoFields.label: Applicant's name
demoFields.hint: As on your Aadhaar.

demoFields.label: Male or female
demoFields.hint: Tick or write one.

demoFields.label: Father's or husband's name
demoFields.hint: Husband's name for a married woman or a widow, father's name otherwise.

demoFields.label: Full postal address (present and permanent)
demoFields.value: Door no. 7, Hosahalli, Sira taluk, Tumakuru 572137
demoFields.hint: Write both if you live away from your permanent home.

demoFields.label: Age on the date of application
demoFields.hint: Write which age proof you are attaching.

demoFields.label: Pension applied for
demoFields.hint: Tick one box: old age, widow, disability, Sandhya Suraksha, Manaswini, Maithri, acid attack victim, farmer's widow or endosulfan victim.

demoFields.label: Family's annual income
demoFields.hint: Must be below Rs.32,000. Attach the income certificate.

demoFields.label: Combined deposits of husband and wife
demoFields.value: Rs.4,500, savings account, Sira branch of a co-operative bank
demoFields.hint: Amount, type of deposit and the bank. For Sandhya Suraksha it must not be above Rs.10,000.

demoFields.label: Any other pension, and occupation
demoFields.value: No other pension; farm labourer (Tahsildar's certificate attached)
demoFields.hint: Another pension makes you ineligible. The occupation certificate is needed for Sandhya Suraksha.

demoSteps: Download the common pension form from dssp.karnataka.gov.in, or ask for it at the Nadakacheri counter.
Fill it in, tick the pension you want, sign or put your left thumb impression, and attach the documents.
Hand it in at the Atalji Janasnehi Kendra for your hobli or taluk, and keep the acknowledgement number.
The village administrative officer and the revenue inspector check your age, income and residence, often with a home visit. The Tahsildar then sanctions the pension.
The pension order gives you a beneficiary ID. The pension is then paid every month into your bank or post office account.

Check the status, or a stopped payment, on the Beneficiary Status page of dssp.karnataka.gov.in with your beneficiary ID. If payments stop, first make sure your account is seeded with Aadhaar, then go to the taluk office.
schemes.helpline: 080-22232040 / 080-22232012 — Directorate of Social Security and Pensions, Bengaluru; 1902 — Karnataka government citizen helpline
